dimensions.evidence: Expression 1 + R adds pure number 1 to dimensionless rate R (per-individual per-period), yielding dimensionless multiplier L. Source units 'individuals/individual/year' cancel to per-period; both variables declared dimensionless/unit 1. Consistent.

guards-inverses.evidence: Guard R >= -1 is correct (R=-1 gives L=0, total loss in one interval; R<-1 would give negative multiplier). Rejection cases cover R=-1.5 (domain) and missing R. Inverse R = L - 1 verified by substitution (L=1.1 -> R=0.1 matches published example). BUT limitation 1 claims the ratio inversion L = N2/N1 is 'documented in the inverse notes' while inverse_notes contain no N2/N1 step, so a claimed inverse branch is cited as documented but absent. The source page does support ratio estimation ('lambda is the ratio of the population size at one time to its size one time-unit earlier'), so the defect is the false internal cross-reference, not the science.
